title: The criminal trade in ancient objects
speaker: BBC Learning English

sentences.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 你好,这是6分钟英语 从英国广播公司学习英语。

sentences.en: I'm Neil. And I'm Beth. Neil, what is the oldest thing you have at home?
sentences.zh: 我是尼尔 我是贝丝 尼尔 你家里最古老的东西是什么?

sentences.en: Ooh… well, I do have some books from when I was a child.
sentences.zh: 哦... 好吧,我确实有一些书 当我还是个孩子。

sentences.en: I have a rocking horse that was my dad's, so that is quite old.
sentences.zh: 我有一匹是我爸的摇摆马 所以那已经很老了

sentences.en: But neither of these are anywhere near as old as the 1,800-year-old Roman coin which BBC reporter Ryan Keane recently bought in London.
sentences.zh: 但这两个都不像英国广播公司记者赖安·基恩最近在伦敦买的1800年罗马硬币那么古老。

sentences.en: But soon afterwards, Ryan discovered there was more to the story, as he explains here on BBC World Service programme Business Daily: But as I researched into other kinds of ancient artefacts I could acquire, I came across reports of expansive criminal networks related to antiquities.
sentences.zh: 但不久之后,Ryan发现这个故事更多, 正如他在BBC世界服务节目《商业日报》上所解释的: 但是,当我研究其他种类的古老文物时, 我发现了关于与古董有关的广泛犯罪网络的报道。

sentences.en: Some ancient artefacts being sold online and in stores have been looted and trafficked.
sentences.zh: 一些在网上和商店出售的古老文物被洗劫和贩运。

sentences.en: Ryan got interested in artefacts from Egypt, Greece and Rome.
sentences.zh: 瑞安对埃及、希腊和罗马的手工艺品感兴趣

sentences.en: An artefact is any object made by humans, usually very old, which is historically interesting – for example, a coin or statue.
sentences.zh: 艺术品是人类制造的任何物品,通常非常古老,这在历史上是有趣的,例如硬币或雕像。

sentences.en: In the past, many artefacts have been looted – or stolen by force.
sentences.zh: 过去,许多手工艺品被抢掠或被抢走。

sentences.en: Movies like Indiana Jones and Tomb Raider have made the subject popular, but the theft of ancient objects is a serious problem in some parts of the world.
sentences.zh: 印第安纳·琼斯和汤姆·雷德尔等电影使这个主题受到欢迎,但盗窃古代文物是世界一些地区的一个严重问题。

sentences.en: So, what can be done about it? That's what we'll be discussing in this episode, using some useful new words and phrases.
sentences.zh: 那么,可以做些什么呢?这就是我们在这个集中要讨论的, 使用一些有用的新词和短语。

sentences.en: And remember – you'll find all the vocabulary from this episode on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 并记住-你会在我们的网站上找到这集的词汇,bbc学习英语.com。

sentences.en: Now, I have a question for you, Beth. One of the most famous ancient artefacts was discovered by Egyptologist Howard Carter in the Valley of the Kings in 1922, but what was it?
sentences.zh: 贝丝,我有一个问题要问你。 最著名的古代文物之一 是埃及学家霍华德·卡特在1922年在国王谷发现的,但是什么?

sentences.en: Was it: a) the Rosetta Stone, b) the Mask of Tutankhamun, or c) the Ark of the Covenant?
sentences.zh: (a) 罗塞塔石,(b) 图坦卡蒙的面具,(c) 《盟约》的方舟?

sentences.en: Oh, I think it's b) the Mask of Tutankhamun.
sentences.zh: 哦,我想这是b) 图坦卡蒙的面具。

sentences.en: OK. Let's find out later in the programme.
sentences.zh: 好吧 我们稍后在节目里查查

sentences.en: Stealing ancient objects is nothing new.
sentences.zh: 盗取古老的物体并不是什么新鲜事。

sentences.en: During colonial times, it was common for artefacts to be taken from their original home and moved to museums and private collections abroad.
sentences.zh: 在殖民时代,艺术品通常从原住地运到国外博物馆和私人收藏。

sentences.en: In the modern era, technology, especially social media, has increased the problem.
sentences.zh: 在现代,技术,特别是社会媒体,加剧了这一问题。

sentences.en: Here's, Amr Al-Azm, a researcher from Shawnee State University in the US, explaining more to BBC's Business Daily: Social media is the game changer here.
sentences.zh: 这是Amr Al-Azm, 来自美国Shawnee州立大学的研究员, 向英国广播公司的《商业日报》解释更多:社交媒体是这里的游戏改变者。

sentences.en: The bottleneck, if you will, was how does someone who has an item then communicate with someone on the demand side?
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意的话, 瓶颈是, 一个人谁有一件东西 然后与人交流 在需求方?

sentences.en: It used to slow the process – you had to go through intermediaries.
sentences.zh: 它曾经拖慢过程——你必须通过中间人。

sentences.en: Social media changes all that because it just opens it up.
sentences.zh: 社交媒体改变了这一切 因为它只是打开它。

sentences.en: Amr calls social media a game changer – something new that is introduced into a situation and completely changes how it works.
sentences.zh: Amr称社交媒体为游戏变革者,

sentences.en: For example, the internet has been a game changer in how we communicate.
sentences.zh: 例如,互联网改变了我们沟通的方式。

sentences.en: The reason is simple. For someone with illegally stolen artefacts to sell, finding a buyer used to be difficult.
sentences.zh: 原因很简单,对于非法盗窃物品的人来说,很难找到买主。

sentences.en: Amr thinks that now, because of social media, this problem, or bottleneck, is gone.
sentences.zh: Amr认为,现在,由于社交媒体, 这个问题,或瓶颈,已经消失。

sentences.en: A bottleneck is a problem that delays a process or stops it from progressing.
sentences.zh: 瓶颈是一个拖延进程或阻止进程进展的问题。

sentences.en: So, what can be done to stop the illegal buying and selling of ancient artefacts?
sentences.zh: 那么,可以做些什么来阻止非法买卖古代文物?

sentences.en: Well, as the final destination for much looted treasure, museums have an important role to play.
sentences.zh: 作为大肆掠夺的宝藏的最终目的地,博物馆可以发挥重要作用。

sentences.en: Accusations of knowingly or unknowingly buying stolen objects have been made against several museums, including the Louvre in Paris.
sentences.zh: 对包括巴黎卢浮宫在内的若干博物馆提出了知情或无意购买被盗物品的指控。

sentences.en: Victoria Reed is senior curator at the Museum of Fine Arts in Boston.
sentences.zh: 维多利亚·里德是波士顿美术博物馆的高级馆长。

sentences.en: In 2024, she helped her museum return an ancient necklace which had been taken illegally from Turkey in the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 2024年,她帮助博物馆归还了一条古老的项链,这条项链是1970年代从土耳其非法拿走的。

sentences.en: But the idea of returning artefacts to their country of origin, something known as repatriation, is controversial, as Victora told BBC programme Business Daily: Outside of the museum world, of course, there are many opinions, and I personally try to maintain a relatively middle-of-the-road approach.
sentences.zh: 但是,将艺术品送回原籍国的想法,即所谓遣返的想法是有争议的,正如维克多拉告诉英国广播公司的节目《商业日报》:当然,在博物馆世界之外有许多观点,我个人试图保持相对中途的做法。

sentences.en: I believe in museums, I believe in responsible collecting and I believe in judicious repatriation decisions.
sentences.zh: 我相信博物馆,我相信负责的收集,我相信明智的遣返决定。

sentences.en: There are arguments both for and against repatriating artefacts, and Victoria takes a middle-of-the-road approach.
sentences.zh: 无论是支持还是反对遣返文物,维多利亚都采取了中途办法。

sentences.en: If you describe something as middle-of-the-road, you mean it's not extreme and is acceptable to most people.
sentences.zh: 如果你把某种东西描述为中路, 你的意思是它不是极端的,是大多数人都能接受的。

sentences.en: Whether ancient artefacts find their way back to their original homes or are displayed in museums remains an ongoing debate, but either way it's good to know that objects of culture and beauty are being preserved for future generations.
sentences.zh: 古代文物是回到原居地还是展出在博物馆里, 仍然是一场持续的辩论, 但无论哪种方式, 都很好地知道, 文化和美的物品 被保存在后代。

sentences.en: OK. I think it's time to reveal the answer to my question.
sentences.zh: 好吧,我想是时候 透露我的问题的答案了

sentences.en: I asked what the Egyptologist Howard Carter discovered in the Valley of the Kings in 1922.
sentences.zh: 我问埃及学家霍华德·卡特 1922年在国王谷发现了什么

sentences.en: Was it: a) the Rosetta Stone, b) the Mask of Tutankhamun, or c) the Ark of the Covenant?
sentences.zh: (a) 罗塞塔石,(b) 图坦卡蒙的面具,(c) 《盟约》的方舟?

sentences.en: And I said, "The Mask of Tutankhamun." And you, Beth… were right.
sentences.zh: 我说"图坦卡蒙的面具" 而你 贝丝 是对的

sentences.en: Yes! OK. Let's recap the vocabulary we've learned, starting with artefact – any object made by humans which is of historical interest.
sentences.zh: 是的!好。让我们回顾一下我们所学的词汇,从人造物开始-- 任何人类制造的具有历史意义的物品。

sentences.en: If something is looted, it's stolen by force.
sentences.zh: 如果什么东西被抢了,它被抢走了。

sentences.en: A game changer is a new element which, when introduced into a situation, completely changes it.
sentences.zh: 游戏变换器是一个新元素, 当引入一个环境时, 它会完全改变它 。

sentences.en: A bottleneck is a problem that delays a process or stops it from progressing.
sentences.zh: 瓶颈是一个拖延进程或阻止进程进展的问题。

sentences.en: To repatriate something means to return it to the country it came from.
sentences.zh: 将一些东西送回来 意味着将它送回来的国家

sentences.en: And finally, the adjective middle-of-the-road describes things which are not extreme and are acceptable to most people.
sentences.zh: 最后,中间道路的形容词描述了一些非极端和大多数人都能接受的事情。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up. If you enjoyed this programme, why not check out the accompanying worksheet and quiz?
sentences.zh: 再说一遍,我们六分钟就到了。如果你喜欢这个节目,为什么不看看随附的工作表和测验表呢?

sentences.en: They're both available now at bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 他们现在都在bbc学习英语.com。

sentences.en: See you there soon and goodbye. Goodbye!
sentences.zh: 再见 再见!
